newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares end firmer after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares end firmer after U.S. data.

text.p: 1430 GMT - Swiss shares ended with slight advances, edging above the psychologically important level of 3,800 points in the Swiss Market Index (SMI) after U.S. producer prices and retail sales data buoyed the market in late trade.

"We had a very quiet day although the U.S. data were positive," a trader said. He added that fundamentals remained good but next week's development may be shaky because several warrants on numerous SMI shares will expire on October 18.
* The SMI ended up 0.21 percent, or 7.9 points, at 3,805.2.
* All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 5.26 points, or 0.22 percent, to 2,435.79.
* Pharmaceuticals Roche, Ciba and Sandoz gained ground after Thursday's losses. Roche certificates rose 55 francs to 9,585.

* UBS bearer shares continued to gain on foreign buying interest, ading seven francs to 1,257. Traders cited expectations in the market that UBS may sooner or later announce a restructuring as rivals CS Holding and SBC have already done.

* CS Holding slipped one franc to 127. Shareholders approved a name change to Credit Suiss Group as of January 1, 1997 at an extraordinary meeting. Chairman Rainer Gut reiterated he expected group profit to rise in 1996.
* Swiss Re lost two francs to 1,353.

* SMH bearer shares were slightly higher after Thursday's slump of nearly three percent. Standard & Poor's Market Scope on Thursday issued a sell note following a review of the Smart Car project, a micro car developed by SMH and Daimler Benz. SMH head Nicolas Hayek rejected the report's conclusions.
* Alusuisse rose two francs to 941 francs after recent lows.
* ABB, which named a new chief executive on Thursday, ended flat at 1,557 francs.
* Second-tier insurer Berner Holding added 18 francs to 870.
